```{python}
PAL = px.colors.qualitative.Safe


def show(fig, height=450, **kw):

                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.2), **kw)

def md(text):

def table(df, **kw):
    display(HTML(df.to_html(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.4g}", **kw)))


runs = {}
for d in sorted((RUN / "runs").glob("*/")):

        runs[d.name] = dict(meta=json.loads((d / "run.json").read_text()),

gids = next(iter(runs.values()))["cell"]["community"]
own = {r: ("fba" if v["meta"]["ceq"] is None else f"ceq={v['meta']['ceq']}") for r, v in runs.items()}
cx = {k: pd.read_csv(RUN / "crosseval" / f"{k}.csv") if (RUN / "crosseval" / f"{k}.csv").exists() and (RUN / "crosseval" / f"{k}.csv").stat().st_size > 1
      else pd.DataFrame() for k in ("media", "links", "spent", "fluxes", "robust")}
```

## How to read this

Each run is one `cfs interactions` search (design spec §13.5) for one **arm** (the
model: plain FBA, or FBA with thermodynamic product inhibition at a given `c^eq`),
one **objective**, and one medium-draw **seed**:

- **handover** maximises `E = Σ_m min(secretion, uptake)`: mass one member makes
  and the other takes up. Positive interaction only.
- **interference** maximises the growth-rate loss each member suffers from its
  partner at the same medium: competition plus product inhibition.
- **conditioning** (inhibited arms only) looks for media where a partner's
  *products* hurt growth, with what it consumed put back.

The search proposes with the surrogate and accepts with the true LP, so every
"true" number is an LP solve; every "hat" number is the surrogate. Abundances are
uniform (`X = 1` each), so rates are per unit biomass and are capacities of the
medium, not predictions of an assembled community. Growth rates use the GEMs'
`|Vmax| = 1000` uptake bounds and are ~30× physiological (CLAUDE.md, "Per-organism
`Vmax`"); compare them with each other, not with a stopwatch.

## What the searches' screens found

Every medium a run screened (its random draws plus the candidate media built to
open each possible handover) was solved with the **true LP**, one solve per
member. A handover is a metabolite one member secretes and the other takes up at
the same medium; its rate is `min(secreted, taken up)`, in mmol/gDW/h at equal
biomass. Identical media screened by several runs are counted once.

```{python}
BUF = {"EX_h_e", "EX_h2o_e"}  # buffered by the vessel, never interactions


def nm(m):
    return m.removeprefix("EX_").removesuffix("_e")


pools = {}
for r, v in runs.items():
    z = np.load(RUN / "runs" / r / "media.npz", allow_pickle=True)
    if "pool_c" not in z or "pool_z_true_0" not in z:
        continue
    pools[r] = dict(
        c=z["pool_c"], variant=z["pool_variant"], target=z["pool_metabolite"],
        Z=z["pool_z_true_0"], ex=[str(x) for x in z["exchanges"]],
        starts=[int(d["start_draw"]) for d in v["cell"]["designs"]], c_design=z["c_design"],
    )


def handovers(Z, ex):
    """[(metabolite, producer, consumer, secreted, taken up, rate)] at one medium."""
    out = []
    sec, upt = np.clip(Z, 0, None), np.clip(-Z, 0, None)
    rate = np.minimum(sec.sum(0), upt.sum(0))
    for j in np.flatnonzero(rate > 1e-6):
        if ex[j] in BUF:
            continue
        p, q = int(np.argmax(sec[:, j])), int(np.argmax(upt[:, j]))
        out.append((ex[j], gids[p], gids[q], sec[p, j], upt[q, j], rate[j]))
    return out


if not pools:
    md("_These runs predate the saved screening pool; re-run INTERACTIONS to get the true-LP survey._")
else:
    rows, seen = [], set()
    for r, p in pools.items():
        arm = runs[r]["meta"]["arm"]
        for i in range(len(p["c"])):
            key = (arm, p["c"][i].round(12).tobytes())
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            for m, a, b, s, u, e in handovers(p["Z"][i], p["ex"]):
                rows.append(dict(arm=arm, medium=len(seen), metabolite=nm(m), producer=a, consumer=b,
                                 secreted=s, taken_up=u, rate=e))
    SV = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    n_media = pd.Series([k[0] for k in seen]).value_counts()
    sv = (SV.groupby(["arm", "metabolite", "producer", "consumer"])
          .agg(media=("medium", "nunique"), median_rate=("rate", "median"), max_rate=("rate", "max"))
          .reset_index())
    sv["pct_media"] = 100 * sv.media / sv.arm.map(n_media)
    sv["link"] = sv.metabolite + ":  " + sv.producer + " → " + sv.consumer
    md("Screened media per arm: " + ", ".join(f"**{a}** {n}" for a, n in n_media.items()) + ".")
    top = sv.groupby("link").pct_media.max().nlargest(30).index[::-1]
    fig = px.bar(sv[sv.link.isin(top)], y="link", x="pct_media", color="arm", barmode="group",
                 orientation="h", color_discrete_sequence=PAL, category_orders={"link": list(top)},
                 hover_data=["media", "median_rate", "max_rate"],
                 labels={"pct_media": "% of screened media where it happens", "link": ""},
                 title="How often each handover happens (true LP, every screened medium)")
    show(fig, height=200 + 22 * len(top))
    table(sv.sort_values(["arm", "pct_media"], ascending=[True, False])
          [["arm", "metabolite", "producer", "consumer", "media", "pct_media", "median_rate", "max_rate"]])
```

## Has the survey converged?

The screens above are the searches' own: 64 random draws per run plus candidate
media built to open each handover, so their counts depend on how many media a run
happened to screen. The **survey** (`survey/<arm>/shard_*.npz`) is separate: media
drawn from the same prior, independent of the search seeds, each solved with the
true LP alone. It answers two questions. *Is the list of handovers complete?* The
accumulation curve should flatten, and the Chao1 estimate of the total number of
handovers should match the number seen. *How often does each one happen?* Its
frequency, with a 95% Wilson interval. Frequencies are relative to this medium
prior, not to any particular natural environment. A handover counts at a medium
when its rate is above 1e-6 (`media`), or, more strictly, when it is at least 1%
of that medium's total `E` (`media_1pct`). To add media, rerun the pipeline with
`-resume` and a larger `--survey_shards`; shard *k* is always the same media.

```{python}
def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    p = k / n
    c, h = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / (1 + z * z / n), z * np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) / (1 + z * z / n)
    return c - h, c + h


SVY = {}
for d in sorted((RUN / "survey").glob("*/")) if (RUN / "survey").exists() else []:
    fs = sorted(d.glob("shard_*.npz"), key=lambda f: int(f.stem.split("_")[1]))
    zs = [np.load(f) for f in fs if f.stat().st_size]
    if zs:
        SVY[d.name] = dict(Z=np.concatenate([z["z"] for z in zs]).astype(float),
                           ex=[str(x) for x in zs[0]["exchanges"]], shards=len(zs))
if not SVY:
    md("_No survey: run the pipeline with this version (SURVEY process)._")
else:
    rows, curves, verdict = [], [], []
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    for arm, s in SVY.items():
        per = []  # per medium: {link: (rate, share of E)}
        for Zm in s["Z"]:
            h = handovers(Zm, s["ex"])
            tot = sum(x[5] for x in h)
            per.append({f"{nm(m)}:  {a} → {b}": (e, e / tot) for m, a, b, _, _, e in h})
        N = len(per)
        links = sorted(set().union(*per))
        first = {lk: next(i for i, p in enumerate(per) if lk in p) for lk in links}
        for lk in links:
            k = sum(lk in p for p in per)
            k1 = sum(lk in p and p[lk][1] >= 0.01 for p in per)
            lo, hi = wilson(k, N)
            rows.append(dict(arm=arm, link=lk, media=k, pct=100 * k / N, ci_lo=100 * lo, ci_hi=100 * hi,
                             media_1pct=k1, pct_1pct=100 * k1 / N,
                             median_rate=np.median([p[lk][0] for p in per if lk in p]), first_seen=first[lk] + 1))
        # accumulation: distinct handovers vs media screened, over random orders
        grid = np.unique(np.geomspace(1, N, 40).astype(int))
        acc = np.array([[len(set().union(*[per[i] for i in o[:n]])) for n in grid]
                        for o in (rng.permutation(N) for _ in range(30))])
        curves += [dict(arm=arm, media=n, mean=m, lo=a, hi=b)
                   for n, m, a, b in zip(grid, acc.mean(0), np.percentile(acc, 5, 0), np.percentile(acc, 95, 0), strict=True)]
        cnt = np.array([sum(lk in p for p in per) for lk in links])
        f1, f2 = int((cnt == 1).sum()), int((cnt == 2).sum())
        chao = len(links) + f1 * (f1 - 1) / (2 * (f2 + 1))
        late = sum(first[lk] >= 0.75 * N for lk in links)
        widest = max((wilson(c, N)[1] - wilson(c, N)[0]) / 2 for c in cnt) if len(cnt) else 0
        verdict.append(dict(arm=arm, media=N, shards=s["shards"], handovers=len(links), singletons=f1,
                            doubletons=f2, chao1=round(chao, 1), new_in_last_quarter=late,
                            widest_ci_half_width_pct=round(100 * widest, 1),
                            converged=bool(late == 0 and chao - len(links) < 0.5)))
    SR = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    md("**Convergence per arm.** `converged` = no handover first seen in the last quarter of the "
       "media and Chao1 within 0.5 of the number seen. Singletons (seen once) are what Chao1 "
       "extrapolates from; a list with many of them is still growing.")
    table(pd.DataFrame(verdict))
    fig = go.Figure()
    for k, (arm, c) in enumerate(pd.DataFrame(curves).groupby("arm")):
        col = PAL[k % len(PAL)]
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=c.media, y=c.hi, line=dict(width=0), showlegend=False, hoverinfo="skip"))
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=c.media, y=c.lo, fill="tonexty", line=dict(width=0), fillcolor=col,
                                 opacity=0.25, showlegend=False, hoverinfo="skip"))
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=c.media, y=c["mean"], name=arm, line=dict(color=col)))
    fig.update_layout(title="Distinct handovers found vs media screened (mean, 5-95% over 30 random orders)",
                      xaxis=dict(title="media screened", type="log"), yaxis_title="distinct handovers")
    show(fig)
    top = SR.groupby("link").pct.max().sort_values().index
    fig = px.scatter(SR, y="link", x="pct", color="arm", error_x=SR.ci_hi - SR.pct, error_x_minus=SR.pct - SR.ci_lo,
                     color_discrete_sequence=PAL, category_orders={"link": list(top)[::-1]},
                     hover_data=["media", "media_1pct", "median_rate", "first_seen"],
                     labels={"pct": "% of survey media (95% Wilson interval)", "link": ""},
                     title="How often each handover happens over the survey (true LP)")
    show(fig, height=200 + 22 * len(top))
    table(SR.sort_values(["arm", "pct"], ascending=[True, False]))

    # Which handovers the model itself creates or destroys, at *independently drawn*
    # media. Each run's `inhibition_only_links` answers the same question at that
    # run's own designed medium, and the arms' optima are different media, so that
    # version is confounded by the design -- here it disagrees with itself across
    # seeds. The survey is the unconfounded comparison: the same prior, 4-figure n,
    # and the arms differ only in the bound.
    ref = "fba" if "fba" in set(SR.arm) else sorted(set(SR.arm))[0]
    N = dict(zip(pd.DataFrame(verdict).arm, pd.DataFrame(verdict).media, strict=True))
    if len(N) > 1:
        wide = SR.pivot_table(index="link", columns="arm", values=["media", "pct", "ci_lo", "ci_hi"]).fillna(0)
        cmp = []
        for arm in sorted(set(SR.arm) - {ref}):
            for lk in wide.index:
                a, b = wide.loc[lk, ("pct", ref)], wide.loc[lk, ("pct", arm)]
                disjoint = (wide.loc[lk, ("ci_hi", ref)] < wide.loc[lk, ("ci_lo", arm)]
                            or wide.loc[lk, ("ci_hi", arm)] < wide.loc[lk, ("ci_lo", ref)])
                cmp.append(dict(arm=arm, link=lk, pct_ref=a, pct_arm=b, delta_pct=b - a,
                                fold=(b / a if a else float("inf")) if b else 0.0,
                                media_ref=int(wide.loc[lk, ("media", ref)]),
                                media_arm=int(wide.loc[lk, ("media", arm)]),
                                verdict=("created" if a == 0 and b > 0 else "destroyed" if b == 0 and a > 0
                                         else ("promoted" if b > a else "demoted") if disjoint else "same"),
                                ci_disjoint=bool(disjoint)))
        CMP = pd.DataFrame(cmp).sort_values(["arm", "delta_pct"], ascending=[True, False])
        md(f"**What the model changes, at the same medium prior.** Each arm against **{ref}**, over "
           + ", ".join(f"{a} {n}" for a, n in N.items()) + " media. `created`/`destroyed`: present in "
           "one arm and never in the other. `promoted`/`demoted`: both happen, and the 95% Wilson "
           "intervals do not overlap. `same`: the intervals overlap, so this survey cannot "
           "separate them. An arm that changes a handover's *frequency* by orders of magnitude is "
           "the §13.11 result — the two models disagree about which medium to run.")
        table(CMP)
        big = CMP[CMP.verdict.isin(["created", "destroyed", "promoted", "demoted"])]
        if not big.empty:
            md("Changed: " + "; ".join(f"**{r.link}** {r.verdict} ({r.pct_ref:.2f}% → {r.pct_arm:.2f}%"
                                       f" under {r.arm})" for r in big.itertuples()) + ".")
        else:
            md("No handover's frequency separates between the arms at 95%.")
    if pools:
        srch = {(runs[r]["meta"]["arm"], f"{nm(m)}:  {a} → {b}")
                for r, p in pools.items() for Zm in p["Z"] for m, a, b, *_ in handovers(Zm, p["ex"])}
        only = sorted(srch - {(r.arm, r.link) for r in SR.itertuples()})
        md("**Found in the searches' screens but never in the survey** (reachable only from the "
           "constructed candidate media, or too rare for the survey to have hit): "
           + (", ".join(f"{lk} ({a})" for a, lk in only) if only else "none."))
```

## The interactions at the designed media

Each run's best designed medium, solved with the true LP under the run's own model.
`share of E` is that metabolite's fraction of the total handover rate `E`.

```{python}
FX = cx["fluxes"]
if FX.empty:
    md("_No `fluxes.csv`: re-run CROSSEVAL with this version of the pipeline._")
else:
    FX["own"] = [own.get(r) == m for r, m in zip(FX.run, FX.model, strict=True)]
    FX["label"] = FX.metabolite.map(nm)
    D = FX[FX.own & FX.best & FX.medium.eq("design")]
    H = D[D.handover > 1e-6]
    E_run = H.drop_duplicates(["run", "metabolite"]).groupby("run").handover.sum()
    p = H.pivot_table(index=["run", "arm", "objective", "metabolite", "handover"],
                      columns="member", values="z").reset_index()
    p["producer"] = np.where(p[gids[0]] > 0, gids[0], gids[1])
    p["consumer"] = np.where(p[gids[0]] > 0, gids[1], gids[0])
    p["secreted"] = p[gids].max(axis=1)
    p["taken_up"] = -p[gids].min(axis=1)
    p["share"] = p.handover / p.run.map(E_run)
    cons = (p.groupby(["metabolite", "producer", "consumer"])
            .agg(runs=("run", "nunique"), arms=("arm", lambda s: ", ".join(sorted(set(s)))),
                 secreted=("secreted", "median"), taken_up=("taken_up", "median"),
                 handover=("handover", "median"), share_of_E=("share", "median"))
            .reset_index().sort_values(["runs", "handover"], ascending=False))
    cons["metabolite"] = cons.metabolite.map(nm)
    cons["share_of_E"] = (100 * cons.share_of_E).round(1).astype(str) + "%"
    md(f"**Handovers at the {p.run.nunique()} designed media** (medians over the runs where each occurs; "
       "`secreted` / `taken_up` are the producer's and consumer's own fluxes, so the handover is capped "
       "by the smaller):")
    table(cons)
```

```{python}
def member_bars(frames, xlabel, hover_extra):
    """One diverging bar chart per run (dropdown): secretion right, uptake left, one bar per member."""
    names = list(frames)
    fig = go.Figure()
    for i, r in enumerate(names):
        d = frames[r]
        for k, g in enumerate(gids):
            dd = d[d.member.eq(g)]
            fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
                y=dd.ylab, x=dd.z, orientation="h", name=g, legendgroup=g, visible=i == 0,
                showlegend=True, marker_color=PAL[k], customdata=dd[hover_extra].to_numpy(),
                hovertemplate=f"{g}<br>%{{y}}<br>flux %{{x:.4g}} mmol/gDW/h"
                              + "".join(f"<br>{h} %{{customdata[{n}]:.4g}}" for n, h in enumerate(hover_extra))
                              + "<extra></extra>"))
    cats = {r: list(frames[r].sort_values("order").ylab.unique()) for r in names}
    tr = len(gids)
    fig.update_layout(
        barmode="group", xaxis_title=xlabel, title=names[0],
        yaxis=dict(categoryorder="array", categoryarray=cats[names[0]]),
        updatemenus=[dict(x=1, y=1.12, xanchor="right", buttons=[
            dict(label=r, method="update",
                 args=[{"visible": [k // tr == i for k in range(tr * len(names))]},
                       {"title.text": r, "yaxis.categoryarray": cats[r]}])
            for i, r in enumerate(names)])])
    fig.add_vline(x=0, line_color="grey")
    return fig, max(len(c) for c in cats.values())


if not FX.empty:
    fr = {}
    for r, d in H.groupby("run"):
        d = d.assign(share=d.handover / E_run[r])
        d["ylab"] = (d.label + ": handover " + d.handover.map("{:.3g}".format)
                     + " (" + (100 * d.share).round(1).astype(str) + "% of E)")
        d["order"] = d.handover  # categoryarray is bottom-up, so the largest ends on top
        fr[r] = d
    fig, n = member_bars(fr, "← taken up      flux (mmol/gDW/h)      secreted →", ["handover", "share"])
    md("**Who makes and who takes each handed-over metabolite**, per run (pick it from the menu). "
       "Bars to the right are secretion, to the left uptake; the handover is the smaller of the two, "
       "and its rate is in the label.")
    show(fig, height=180 + 40 * n)
```

```{python}
if not FX.empty:
    fr = {}
    for r, d in D.groupby("run"):
        mx = d.groupby("metabolite").z.apply(lambda s: s.abs().max())
        keep_m = set(mx.nlargest(30).index) | set(d.metabolite[d.handover > 1e-6])
        d = d[d.metabolite.isin(keep_m)].copy()
        d["ylab"] = np.where(d.handover > 1e-6, "⇄ ", "") + d.label
        d["order"] = d.metabolite.map(mx)
        d["growth"] = d.mu
        fr[r] = d
    fig, n = member_bars(fr, "← taken up      flux (mmol/gDW/h)      secreted →", ["handover", "growth"])
    md("**Each member's whole exchange with the medium** at the designed medium: the 30 largest fluxes "
       "plus every handover (`⇄`). This is what each member eats and what it releases, whether or not "
       "the partner uses it. Hover shows the member's growth rate `μ` (1/h).")
    show(fig, height=180 + 22 * n)
```

### Is each handover real?

Four checks on every handover at each run's best design, under the run's own
model. The first three are new true-LP solves; the last needs none.

- **Seeds**: in how many of the independent seeds of that arm and objective the
  handover appears at the best design. Each seed draws its own random media, and
  its own background for the candidate media (whose targets come from the labels).
- **Forced**: the reported fluxes are one optimum (the elastic-net QP's), but most
  exchanges have many optima (M1: 69%). FVA with growth held at its maximum gives
  the rate *every* optimum delivers. `forced` = more than 99% of the rate is
  guaranteed, `tie-break` = under 1%, so the handover is the QP's choice, not the
  network's. `forced@0.95` is the same at 95% of maximum growth: how much the
  handover depends on growing exactly optimally.
- **eps**: the rate when the QP is re-solved at the labels' other two
  elastic-net weights (1e-2, 1e-4), relative to the reported one (1e-3).
- **Abundance**: the handover's share of `E` as the first member's biomass goes
  from 1/10 to 10x the second's. Each member's fluxes do not depend on the
  partner's biomass, so this only changes which side caps the rate.

```{python}
RB = cx["robust"]
if RB.empty:
    md("_No `robust.csv`: re-run CROSSEVAL with this version of the pipeline._")
else:
    RB = RB[[own.get(r) == m for r, m in zip(RB.run, RB.model, strict=True)]].copy()
    RB["eps_lo"] = RB[[c for c in RB if c.startswith("rate@eps=")]].min(axis=1) / RB.rate
    xs = [c for c in RB if c.startswith("share@X=")]
    RB["share_lo"], RB["share_hi"] = RB[xs].min(axis=1), RB[xs].max(axis=1)
    RB["forced95"] = RB["forced_rate@0.95"] / RB.rate
    n_seeds = ov.groupby(["arm", "objective"]).seed.nunique()
    rc = (RB.groupby(["arm", "objective", "metabolite", "producer", "consumer"])
          .agg(seeds=("seed", "nunique"), rate=("rate", "median"), share=("share", "median"),
               forced=("forced_frac", "median"), forced_0_95=("forced95", "median"),
               classes=("class", lambda s: ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in s.value_counts().items())),
               eps_worst=("eps_lo", "min"), share_X_lo=("share_lo", "min"), share_X_hi=("share_hi", "max"))
          .reset_index())
    rc["seeds"] = (rc.seeds.astype(str) + "/"
                   + [str(n_seeds[(a, o)]) for a, o in zip(rc.arm, rc.objective, strict=True)])
    rc["metabolite"] = rc.metabolite.map(nm)
    md("Medians over the seeds where the handover occurs; `eps_worst` and the `share_X` range are "
       "the worst case over them. Read a row as solid when it appears in most seeds, is mostly "
       "`forced`, keeps `eps_worst` near 1, and keeps a non-trivial share across abundances.")
    table(rc.sort_values(["arm", "objective", "share"], ascending=[True, True, False]))
```

### What the designs are made of, and do the seeds agree?

A design moves ~150-250 metabolites, but its objective is flat along almost all
of them: the search follows the surrogate's gradient and the LP only checks the
objective did not fall, so most moves are drift that changes with the seed. Each
run's best design is therefore **pruned** with the true LP, on the run's *own*
objective (`E` for handover, the growth loss for interference, the conditioning
term for conditioning):

1. each moved metabolite is put back to its start value alone, and the objective
   re-solved (its **contribution**);
2. moves are then reverted cumulatively, cheapest first, as long as the
   objective stays within 1% of the design's;
3. what is left is the start plus the moves that matter.

At the pruned medium the **mechanism** is recorded: the handovers carrying at
least 1% of `E`, and each member's **limiting exchanges** (bounds that bind with
a non-zero reduced cost, as shares of that member's total; "(secretion)" is a
binding product-inhibition bound). Designs are grouped by that signature. A
mechanism that most seeds reach is a result; one seed's mechanism is a lead.
Conditioning runs do not ascend, so their design is the screened start and is
not pruned.

```{python}
PR = [json.loads(f.read_text()) for f in sorted((RUN / "prune").glob("*.json"))
      if f.stat().st_size] if (RUN / "prune").exists() else []
if not PR:
    md("_No `prune/`: re-run the pipeline with this version (PRUNE process)._")
else:
    def short(t):
        # not a blanket replace("_e", ""): `EX_gly_met_e` has one inside the name
        for a, b in (("EX_", ""), ("_e:", ":"), ("_e,", ","), ("_e ", " ")):
            t = t.replace(a, b)
        return t.removesuffix("_e")

    P = pd.DataFrame([dict(run=p["run"], arm=p["arm"], objective=p["objective"], seed=p["seed"],
                           moved=p["n_moved"], kept=p["n_kept"],
                           objective_design=p["objective_design"], objective_pruned=p["objective_pruned"],
                           E_pruned=p["E_pruned"], signature=p["signature"],
                           # The handovers alone are the mechanism this use case is about, and
                           # they are what reproduces: the limiters move with the seed (ties at
                           # the 25% cut are common) and have their own table below, so grouping
                           # on the full signature double-counts them and splits one reproducible
                           # mechanism into one group per seed.
                           handover_set=", ".join(sorted(p["handovers"])) or "no handover")
                      for p in PR])
    n_runs = P.groupby(["arm", "objective"]).run.nunique()

    def groups(key, label):
        G = (P.groupby(["arm", "objective", key])
             .agg(designs=("run", "nunique"), seeds=("seed", lambda s: ", ".join(map(str, sorted(s)))),
                  objective_min=("objective_pruned", "min"), objective_max=("objective_pruned", "max"))
             .reset_index())
        G["share"] = G.designs / [n_runs[(a, o)] for a, o in zip(G.arm, G.objective, strict=True)]
        G[key] = G[key].map(short)
        return (G.rename(columns={key: label})
                .sort_values(["arm", "objective", "designs"], ascending=[True, True, False])
                [["arm", "objective", "designs", "share", "seeds", "objective_min", "objective_max", label]])

    md("**Mechanisms**: designs grouped by the handovers at the pruned design. `share` is the "
       "fraction of that arm and objective's seeds landing on the same set. This is the grouping "
       "to read: the limiters are reported separately below, because they shift with the seed "
       "and including them in the key splits a reproducible handover set into one group per seed.")
    table(groups("handover_set", "handovers"))
    md("The same designs grouped by the **full** signature (handovers | each member's limiters), "
       "for the limiter detail. Expect more groups here; that is the limiters, not the mechanism.")
    table(groups("signature", "signature"))
    md("**Pruning per run**: moves the search made, moves kept, and the objective before and after.")
    table(P.drop(columns="signature").sort_values(["arm", "objective", "seed"]))
    mv = pd.DataFrame([dict(run=p["run"], **m) for p in PR for m in p["moves"] if m["kept"]])
    if not mv.empty:
        hm = mv.pivot_table(index="run", columns="metabolite", values="contribution_rel_pruned")
        fold = mv.pivot_table(index="run", columns="metabolite", values="log10_fold").reindex_like(hm)
        lim = float(np.nanmax(np.abs(hm.to_numpy()))) or 1.0
        fig = go.Figure(go.Heatmap(
            z=hm.to_numpy(), x=[nm(c) for c in hm.columns], y=list(hm.index), customdata=fold.to_numpy(),
            colorscale="RdBu", zmid=0, zmin=-lim, zmax=lim, colorbar=dict(title="share of objective"),
            hovertemplate="%{y}<br>%{x}<br>contribution %{z:.3f} of the objective"
                          "<br>moved %{customdata:+.2f} decades from the start<extra></extra>"))
        fig.update_layout(title="The kept moves: each one's contribution at the pruned design "
                                "(blank = not kept in that run)")
        show(fig, height=150 + 25 * len(hm))
    lm = pd.DataFrame([dict(run=p["run"], arm=p["arm"], objective=p["objective"], member=g, limiter=k, share=v)
                       for p in PR for g, d in p["limiters"].items() for k, v in d.items()])
    if not lm.empty:
        lm["limiter"] = lm.limiter.str.replace("EX_", "").str.replace("_e", "", regex=False)
        lc = (lm[lm.share >= 0.25].groupby(["arm", "objective", "member", "limiter"])
              .agg(runs=("run", "nunique"), median_share=("share", "median")).reset_index())
        lc["of"] = [n_runs[(a, o)] for a, o in zip(lc.arm, lc.objective, strict=True)]
        md("**What limits each member at the pruned designs** (limiters carrying >= 25% of that "
           "member's dual), counted over runs:")
        table(lc.sort_values(["arm", "objective", "member", "runs"], ascending=[True, True, True, False]))
```

## The candidate and designed media

The composition of every medium a run screened, plus its refined designs at the
bottom (pick the run from the menu). Rows are media: `draw` is a random medium;
`uptake`, `uptake+secretion`, `box`, `conditioning@…` etc. are candidate media
built to open a handover of the named metabolite. `★` marks the starts the
search refined. Columns are the candidate targets plus the metabolites whose
concentration varies most across these media (60 at most); the colour is log10
concentration (mM), blank where the metabolite is absent. Every metabolite of every
medium is in `crosseval/media_composition.csv.gz`. The bar on the right is the
total handover rate `E` the true LP finds at that medium; hover it for the
largest handovers.

```{python}
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

if pools:
    M_ = cx["media"]
    names = list(pools)
    fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, shared_yaxes=True, column_widths=[0.86, 0.14],
                        horizontal_spacing=0.01)
    cats, nrows = {}, 0
    for i, r in enumerate(names):
        p = pools[r]
        keep_x = np.array([e not in BUF for e in p["ex"]])
        C = np.vstack([p["c"], p["c_design"]])
        lab = [f"#{k} {v}" + (f": {nm(t)}" if t else "") + (" ★" if k in p["starts"] else "")
               for k, (v, t) in enumerate(zip(p["variant"], p["target"], strict=True))]
        lab += [f"design {k} ← #{s}" for k, s in enumerate(p["starts"])]
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):
            L10 = np.where(C > 0, np.log10(C), np.nan)  # absent = blank, not a colour
        rng = np.nanmax(L10, 0) - np.nanmin(L10, 0) + np.isnan(L10).any(0) * 10.0
        cols = [j for j in np.argsort(-rng) if keep_x[j] and rng[j] > 0.1]
        tgt = {t for t in p["target"] if t}
        cols = ([j for j in cols if p["ex"][j] in tgt]
                + [j for j in cols if p["ex"][j] not in tgt][: max(0, 60 - len(tgt))])
        e_pool, top = [], []
        for k in range(len(p["c"])):
            h = sorted(handovers(p["Z"][k], p["ex"]), key=lambda x: -x[5])
            e_pool.append(sum(x[5] for x in h))
            top.append("<br>".join(f"{nm(m)} {a}→{b} {e:.3g}" for m, a, b, _, _, e in h[:4]) or "none")
        own_d = M_[M_.run.eq(r) & M_.medium.eq("design") & M_.model.eq(own[r])] if not M_.empty else M_
        e_des = [float(own_d.loc[own_d.design.eq(k), "E_true"].iloc[0]) if len(own_d) else np.nan
                 for k in range(len(p["starts"]))]
        e_all = e_pool + e_des
        top += ["(design)"] * len(e_des)
        fig.add_trace(go.Heatmap(z=L10[:, cols], x=[nm(p["ex"][j]) for j in cols], y=lab, visible=i == 0,
                                 colorscale="Viridis", colorbar=dict(title="log10 c", x=1.02),
                                 hovertemplate="%{y}<br>%{x}<br>log10 c = %{z:.2f}<extra></extra>"),
                      row=1, col=1)
        fig.add_trace(go.Bar(y=lab, x=e_all, orientation="h", visible=i == 0, customdata=top,
                             marker_color=["#888888"] * len(e_pool) + ["#CC6677"] * len(e_des),
                             showlegend=False,
                             hovertemplate="%{y}<br>E = %{x:.4g}<br>%{customdata}<extra></extra>"),
                      row=1, col=2)
        nrows = max(nrows, len(lab))
    fig.update_layout(
        title=names[0], xaxis2_title="E (true LP)", yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed", tickfont=dict(size=8)),
        updatemenus=[dict(x=1, y=1.0, yanchor="bottom", xanchor="right", buttons=[
            dict(label=r, method="update",
                 args=[{"visible": [k // 2 == i for k in range(2 * len(names))]}, {"title.text": r}])
            for i, r in enumerate(names)])])
    fig.update_xaxes(tickfont=dict(size=8), row=1, col=1)
    show(fig, height=max(500, 140 + 9 * nrows))
```

## Same medium, both models

The fixed-medium comparison: every start and designed medium of every run, scored
under plain FBA and under inhibition with the true LP. Points off the diagonal
are where product inhibition changes the interaction *at that medium*; it can go
up as well as down, because `E` is not what the LP maximises.

```{python}
M = cx["media"]
if not M.empty and M.model.nunique() > 1:
    w = M.pivot_table(index=["run", "arm", "objective", "design", "best", "medium"],
                      columns="model", values="E_true").reset_index()
    other = [m for m in M.model.unique() if m != "fba"]
    for m in other:
        fig = px.scatter(w, x="fba", y=m, color="arm", symbol="medium", hover_data=["run", "design", "best"],
                         color_discrete_sequence=PAL, labels={"fba": "E under FBA", m: f"E under {m}"},
                         title=f"Handover rate at the same medium: FBA vs {m}")
        hi = float(np.nanmax(w[["fba", m]].to_numpy())) or 1.0
        fig.add_shape(type="line", x0=0, y0=0, x1=hi, y1=hi, line=dict(dash="dot", color="grey"))
        show(fig)
    mus = [c for c in M.columns if c.startswith("mu:")]
    g = M.melt(id_vars=["run", "arm", "design", "medium", "model"], value_vars=mus,
               var_name="member", value_name="mu")
    g = g.pivot_table(index=["run", "arm", "design", "medium", "member"], columns="model",
                      values="mu").reset_index()
    for m in other:
        fig = px.scatter(g, x="fba", y=m, color="member", symbol="arm", hover_data=["run", "medium"],
                         color_discrete_sequence=PAL, title=f"Growth rate per member: FBA vs {m}")
        show(fig)
```

## Who suppresses whom

The spent-medium assay at each run's best design: grow the donor alone, then grow
the recipient on what is left, against the fresh medium. The change splits into
**depletion** (the donor ate what the recipient needed: competition) and
**conditioning** (what the donor secreted hurts the recipient, with the eaten part
put back: product inhibition). Under plain FBA conditioning is ≥ 0 by
construction. Values are growth-rate changes per hour over a short step, shown on
an `asinh` axis because they span many decades; hover for the raw number.

```{python}
S = cx["spent"]
if S.empty:
    md("_No spent-medium results._")
else:
    S = S.assign(pair=S.donor + " → " + S.recipient)
    s = S.melt(id_vars=["run", "model", "pair"], value_vars=["depletion_per_h", "conditioning_per_h"],
               var_name="term", value_name="per_h")
    s["asinh"] = np.arcsinh(s.per_h)
    fig = px.strip(s, x="pair", y="asinh", color="term", facet_col="model", hover_data=["run", "per_h"],
                   color_discrete_sequence=PAL, stripmode="group",
                   labels={"asinh": "asinh(Δμ per h)"}, title="Directional interference at the designed media")
    show(fig, height=500)
```

## Diagnostics

**Surrogate vs truth, link by link.** Each point is one metabolite at one best
design: the surrogate's handover rate against the LP's. Head B's magnitude is its
weakest axis (P22), so expect scatter in the rate even where the link itself is
right; links on the x-axis floor are ones the surrogate proposed and the LP does
not have.

```{python}
lk = pd.DataFrame([dict(run=r, arm=v["meta"]["arm"], objective=v["meta"]["objective"],
                        metabolite=x["metabolite"], rate_hat=x["rate"], rate_true=x["rate_true"])
                   for r, v in runs.items() for x in v["cell"]["links_at_best_design"]])
floor = 1e-3
lk["rate_true_plot"] = lk.rate_true.clip(lower=floor)
lk["rate_hat_plot"] = lk.rate_hat.clip(lower=floor)
fig = px.scatter(lk, x="rate_hat_plot", y="rate_true_plot", color="arm", symbol="objective",
                 hover_data=["run", "metabolite", "rate_hat", "rate_true"], log_x=True, log_y=True,
                 color_discrete_sequence=PAL, labels={"rate_hat_plot": "surrogate", "rate_true_plot": "true LP"},
                 title=f"Link rates at the best designs (floored at {floor})")
hi = max(lk.rate_hat_plot.max(), lk.rate_true_plot.max())
fig.add_shape(type="line", x0=floor, y0=floor, x1=hi, y1=hi, line=dict(dash="dot", color="grey"))
show(fig)
```

**The surrogate's own survey**, for comparison with the true-LP one above: what
the surrogate *thinks* the pair can exchange over the drawn media. Where it
disagrees with the true-LP survey, believe the LP.

```{python}
surv = pd.DataFrame([dict(arm=v["meta"]["arm"], run=r, **x)
                     for r, v in runs.items() for x in v["cell"]["reachable"]])
agg = (surv.groupby(["arm", "metabolite"])
       .agg(max_rate=("max_rate", "max"), frac_media=("frac_media", "mean"),
            median_rate=("median_rate_when_present", "median")).reset_index())
top = agg.groupby("metabolite")["max_rate"].max().nlargest(30).index
fig = px.bar(agg[agg.metabolite.isin(top)], x="metabolite", y="max_rate", color="arm", barmode="group",
             hover_data=["frac_media", "median_rate"], log_y=True, color_discrete_sequence=PAL,
             category_orders={"metabolite": list(top)},
             title="Top 30 reachable handovers (surrogate, max over drawn media)")
show(fig, height=500)
```

```{python}
d = ov.melt(id_vars=["run", "arm", "objective"], value_vars=["draw_rank_rho", "obj_rank_rho", "magnitude_ratio"])
fig = px.scatter(d, x="variable", y="value", color="arm", symbol="objective", hover_data=["run"],
               color_discrete_sequence=PAL,
               title="Can the surrogate rank media? (rank ρ near 0: only the LP-screened search is worth reading)")
show(fig)
md("`draw_rank_rho`: Spearman(surrogate E, true E) over the drawn media; `obj_rank_rho` the same for the "
   "run's own objective; `magnitude_ratio`: surrogate E / true E at the designed medium (1 = exact; "
   "CLAUDE.md measured 0.45-1.88 for handovers).")
```
